alternatives.name: Side-by-side study
alternatives.plan: Lead with one practical task and direct readers to the Comparator explanation.
alternatives.tradeoff: A concrete reason to visit, with a learning step between the post and the tool.

alternatives.name: Zoom into a detail
alternatives.plan: Lead with close looking and invite readers to see the tool that makes detail study possible.
alternatives.tradeoff: A visually direct message with less emphasis on how two works relate.

alternatives.name: A looking exercise
alternatives.plan: Offer a prompt about what changes when readers compare artworks.
alternatives.tradeoff: Invites curiosity and needs editorial guidance for selecting works.

brief.assumption: We expect a specific visual comparison task to interest art learners. Audience size, baseline click-through rate and demand for the tool require measurement.
brief.audience: Proposed audience of English-reading art learners who already browse museum collections for visual references.

human_review: Confirm the Comparator link and the steps from the information page on mobile before launch.
Clear institutional name and branding use with the museum. If a future version includes artwork, verify its individual asset rights.
Check whether a distinct outbound event for the Comparator can be measured before comparing campaign variants.
brief.market: Proposed international English-language audience for online museum discovery. The campaign points to the museum’s English collection information page.
brief.metric: Outbound click-through rate to the collection information page, measured as clicks divided by post impressions.
brief.objective: Increase clicks from a collection discovery post to the Rijksmuseum page that explains the Comparator.
brief.peer_rationale: The Louvre offers another online collection for people exploring artworks. This comparison concerns audience attention and collection discovery.

peer_source.quote: The Collections database consists of entries for more than 500,000 works
peer_source.scope: The published database covers works from Musée du Louvre and Musée National Eugène-Delacroix. It provides peer context for online collection discovery.

source.quote: Use the Comparator to place artworks side by side and zoom in on the smallest details.

brief.strategy_reason: Side-by-side study matches the published Comparator feature and gives readers one action. If analytics show visits with little follow-through, test the close-looking message.
brief.summary: The Rijksmuseum describes an online Comparator that places artworks side by side and lets visitors zoom into details.

evidence.context: Discover & Create For instance, create your own Collections , which automatically generate an interactive video clip featuring your selected artworks. Use the Comparator to place artworks side by side and zoom in on the smallest details. What will you discover? Share your findings with the rest of the world. Visitors are also welcomed into My Gallery of Honour , a virtual space inspired by the Rijksmuseum's most iconic room. Curate your own Gallery of Honour and tell your story in this legendary setting. Thanks to the Art Explorer , exploring the collection has become even more accessible. This new AI-powered tool invites visitors to answer thought-provoking questions. Their answers lead to surprising and unexpected suggestions from the collection. Please note that the results are unfiltered and may sometimes show unexpectedly shocking and/or explicit images.
